Guides / motivation

How to Keep Going After Slow Progress

Slow progress is easier to tolerate when you can see evidence that the process is still producing information.

A practical method

Return to a baseline, narrow the target, and compare weekly attempts rather than judging each day.

Example

A musician may not hear daily improvement but can compare recordings made two weeks apart.

What to avoid

Do not increase volume blindly when the bottleneck is unclear.

Try this

Compare one current attempt with an older baseline and choose one next adjustment.

Related learning

Continue with the free Learning Hub. For a fuller treatment, Get Good at Anything may be relevant.
